blocks.text: Isaiah 39 belongs to a received book that spans Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, and postexilic horizons. Many scholars therefore understand the book as the result of long collection and editorial development, although no detailed reconstruction has won consensus. The book also uses varied forms and voices—including prophetic speech and third-person royal narrative—so the speaker and literary form need to be identified passage by passage. Its ancient textual transmission is also complex: the Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness broadly aligned with the Masoretic tradition, yet it contains many orthographic and substantive differences.
